# The Crown of the Sky

## Scripture

*"Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades? Can you loosen Orion's belt? Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons?"* — Job 38:31–32

## Reflection

On autumn evenings, the constellation Corona Borealis—the Northern Crown—tips low toward the western horizon, a small semicircle of stars that ancient observers named for its unmistakable curve. It's easy to miss, especially on nights when the brighter summer stars still linger. But there it is: a crown, quietly setting with the season.

Job knew something of crowns being lifted and lowered. He lost everything—wealth, family, health—and in the whirlwind, God didn't offer explanations. He offered questions. *Can you bind the Pleiades? Can you guide the constellations?* The answer, of course, was no. But the One asking could.

There's a strange comfort in autumn's fading crowns. The season teaches us that what we've worn with pride—achievements, reputations, even hard-won identities—can slip toward the horizon. But God's question to Job reminds us that the One who set every crown in the sky also set a crown on Job's head again (Job 42:12). Not because Job deserved it, but because God is faithful to restore.

When your own crown feels low, look west tonight. The Northern Crown isn't gone—just waiting for its season. So are you.

## Prayer

Lord of the constellations, You hold every crown in Your hands—the ones we wear and the ones we've lost. When we feel our light slipping toward the horizon, remind us that You are the One who lifts and restores. Give us patience for the seasons of low light, and hope in Your faithfulness. Amen.
